messages:
Alex K: Quick RFC follow-up on Console dashboards/query layer/RBAC tradeoffs. TL;DR: propose a dedicated read-query service (console-query) that sits between the console frontend and our stores (TSDB + OLAP). It enforces RBAC, does aggregation/caching, and exposes a stable GraphQL-ish query surface. Need alignment on consistency, cost, and rollout plan.

Marta R: Love the separation idea. Two product must-haves: 1) per-organization dashboards must never leak other orgs' metrics, 2) dashboard refresh <= 1s for live views (where possible). Non-live can be eventual.

Jay P: Implementation notes: console-query would be a thin layer that translates UI queries into one of three backends: 1) pre-aggregated materialized views in our OLAP (clickhouse-like), 2) short-window TSDB (prometheus/sidecar) for high-frequency metrics, 3) DB for entity joins (users, teams). We'll keep projections as small JSON blobs to avoid join costs.

Samir G: Ops concerns: adding another service increases blast radius. Need clear SLOs for query latency (p95 < 300ms for cached, p95 < 1.5s for cold). Also must support graceful degradation under load — degrade to cached/approx counts, and surface fallback indicators in the UI.

Chen L: Security comment: RBAC must be enforced at two layers: gateway (deny early) and in console-query (row-level filters). We should avoid trusting frontend ACLs. Proposed token flow: frontend -> Console API (session cookie) -> API Gateway adds X-Org / X-User headers -> console-query verifies KMS-signed service token and applies attribute-based row filter. Example header: `X-Redwood-Auth: org=acme;roles=admin,viewer;sub=user:523`

Nora D: UX note: show stale/approx labels when we fall back. Also we should expose a small metadata field in the response: `{
  "source": "cache|tsdb|olap",
  "stale": true|false,
  "resolution": "15s|1m|5m"
}`

Alex K: Tradeoffs I want to highlight:
- Pros: isolates query load from control plane, allows tailored caching/aggregation and specialized index choices, simpler RBAC model per service.
- Cons: more infra, data duplication, potential consistency lag between time-series and OLAP aggregates, more ownership overhead.

Marta R: For product priorities: start with critical dashboards (cost, latency, errors) and one tenant-mode rollout. If we can hit latency targets for those, expand.

Jay P: Data model suggestion for pre-agg pipeline: hourly/day rollups and a rolling-minute window for the last 30m. Simplified SQL-ish example for materialized view: 
```sql
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW console_metrics_1m AS
SELECT org_id, metric_name, date_trunc('minute', ts) AS minute,
       avg(value) AS avg_v, max(value) AS max_v, sum(count) AS cnt
FROM raw_metrics
GROUP BY org_id, metric_name, minute;
```
We keep the last 30m at 1s-15s resolution in TSDB; 30m-7d in 1m; >7d in 1h.

Samir G: Migration plan idea: start with read-only proxy mode against current stores with an opt-in flag per org. No writes initially. Observability: instrument cache hit rates, query fanout, and RBAC denies.

Chen L: Row-level security detail: store `org_id` on all metric events and enforce `WHERE org_id = :request_org` at the engine level. For more granular per-team data, support attribute filters `team_id IN (...)`. Keep a small policy engine (rego?) inside console-query to evaluate policies quickly.

Alex K: Performance options discussed:
- Local LRU for tiny dashboard cells.
- Redis-based shared cache for larger aggregations with TTLs tuned per metric.
- Continuous query workers to keep hot aggregates warm.

Marta R: Can we define SLOs now? Suggest: cached cell p95 < 250ms, cold-aggregate p95 < 1.2s, under heavy degradation UI shows stale state and 90% graceful fallback.

Jay P: Cost note: materialized views will increase storage but reduce CPU cost on query time. Need to estimate storage delta; I'll run a data sweep next week and post numbers.

Alex K: API contract proposal (minimal): `POST /api/v1/query` body: `{ "org_id": "acme", "query": {"metric":"latency_p50","range":"1h","resolution":"1m"}, "auth": {"user":"u","roles":[]}}` response: payload + metadata (source, stale, resolution). Must return HTTP 403 for RBAC denies.

Nora D: Small ask: add `uiHint` in response to indicate recommended chart type (timeseries | gauge | bar) so front-end can avoid guessing.

arch-bot: New RFC comment: console-query v1: read-only proxy + cache + RBAC enforcement. Link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/console-query-v1

Samir G: Rollout checklist draft:
- telemetry & dashboards for console-query
- canary in staging -> internal orgs
- opt-in tenants in prod (5 initial customers)
- fail-open -> show stale cached widgets if backend unreachable

Chen L: One more: audit logs. Every query that returns non-empty result set must log `org_id, user_id, query_hash, source` to our audit sink. That can be sampled at 1% for cost control but must be configurable per org for compliance customers.

Marta R: Sounds like a plan. Action items?

Alex K: Action items:
- Jay: do data-sweep and cost estimate (due EOD Friday)
- Samir: draft SLOs + degradation behavior (due Mon)
- Chen: RBAC policy sketch (rego prototype) (due Tue)
- Nora: UI metadata fields + stale UX mock (due Tue)
- Marta: pick initial 3 dashboards for v1
I'll put a short RFC follow-up with these items. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Jay P: Ack. I'll share numbers and a rough schema.

Chen L: Will start rego PoC.

Nora D: Mocking now. Will post screenshots soon.

Samir G: Will add an SLO doc and ops runbook.

Alex K: Closing thread — will attach RFC link once I finish edits.
